order: The ranking has zero Canary Islands beaches in tier 1. Across all 594 ES features only 24 are in the Canaries: Tenerife 3, Gran Canaria 2, Lanzarote 6, Fuerteventura 3, La Gomera 10. The Canaries are Spain's largest beach-holiday region by visitor nights and they are effectively missing. This is the single worst ranking defect for the Beaches tab.

Playa de la Malagueta (rank 12) and Playa del Orzán (rank 10) are ordinary working city beaches. They outrank Ses Illetes, Cala Comte, Bolonia, Macarella, Las Teresitas and Maspalomas, none of which appear in tier 1 at all.
Cala de l'Illa Roja at rank 6 is a small unofficially naturist cove reached by a cliff stair. Defensible in a Costa Brava list, not in a national top 6.

Regional clustering is severe. Begur and the Palafrugell coast supply ranks 6, 15, 18, 19, 22, 25, 26 (seven of the top 26 inside about 10 km) and Comillas/San Vicente supply ranks 8, 17, 27, 29. There is no per-region cap.

Praia das Catedrais at rank 3 and Playa de la Concha at rank 2 are correctly high. Es Trenc at rank 1 is a real, protected, genuinely famous beach, so the top of the list is honest even where the middle is not.

Below roughly rank 240 the beach list degenerates into a user-POI dump: emoji names, business names, foreign-language duplicates and a coordinate blob. Anything past rank 200 should not be shipped without a second pass.

missing.name: Teide

missing.name: Montserrat
missing.why: The serrated conglomerate massif and Benedictine abbey above Barcelona, Catalonia's symbolic mountain and one of the most visited natural sites in Spain. Absent from every tier.

missing.name: Roque Nublo
missing.why: The 80 m basalt monolith that is Gran Canaria's emblem, in the Roque Nublo rural park. Absent, while its lower neighbour Pico de las Nieves takes tier 1 rank 11.

missing.name: Pico Almanzor

missing.name: Peñalara

order: Roque de Agando at rank 1 is indefensible as Spain's top mountain. It is a striking volcanic plug on La Gomera, worth listing, but it is not a mountain anyone climbs and it is not what a Spanish mountain card should show. Teide, Mulhacen, Aneto and Montserrat are all absent, so the number one slot went to the most photogenic thing the harvester happened to hold.

Picos de Europa at rank 3 sits directly above and 2.3 km from Torre Cerredo at rank 2, which is its own summit. The range outranks its own high point, and the range card carries a picture of a third mountain that the wire ranks 279th.

The mountain ranking is a map of OpenStreetMap peak density, not of fame. Sixteen of the 279 rows are minor Aiguestortes summits (ranks 14, 15, 23, 24, 33, 34, 38, 45, 46, 47, 53, 54, 55, 56, 57, 58) and a comparable block are unnamed-to-travellers torres in the Picos. One national park with dense OSM coverage outweighs the whole of the Sierra Nevada, which contributes nothing.

Two tier 1 slots are the Gaztelugatxe islet twice and two more are Monte Perdido twice. A third of Spain's tier 1 mountains are duplicates or non-mountains, before counting the football stadium at rank 6.

Puig Major at rank 10 is genuinely Mallorca's highest peak but the summit is an active military radar installation and closed to the public. It should be listed with that caveat rather than presented as a walk.
Monte Perdido at rank 7 and Torre Cerredo at rank 2 are the two entries whose position is straightforwardly correct.

counts_verdict: Twelve tier 1 beaches and twelve tier 1 mountains is far too few for Spain, and the composition matters more than the count. Spain has roughly 8,000 km of coast plus two archipelagos, and the Pyrenees, Sierra Nevada, Picos de Europa, Gredos, Guadarrama, Montserrat and Teide. Compare Malta at 6 beaches: Spain gets twice Malta's allocation for a country with more than a hundred times the coastline and the Canaries on top. Worse, of 594 total features only 24 are in the Canaries (Tenerife 3, Gran Canaria 2, Fuerteventura 3), 5 in Menorca and 7 in Formentera, so no per-region quota can even be met from the current harvest. Spain needs a tier 1 of at least 20 per kind, an explicit per-autonomous-community and per-island quota, and a re-harvest of the Canaries and Menorca before the tab is credible.
top_pick_verdict: top_beach 'Es Trenc Beach' is acceptable: a real, protected, genuinely famous Mallorcan beach with an Excellent EEA class. I would still put Playa de la Concha, San Sebastian, on the country card, because it is the single most recognisable Spanish beach image and it is already ranked 2. top_mountain 'Roque de Agando' is not acceptable and should be rejected outright. Spain's country-card mountain is Teide (Q38954), or Mulhacen (Q209528) if the card is meant to show mainland Spain. Shipping a La Gomera rock pinnacle as Spain's mountain while Teide is absent from the dataset entirely would be the most visible error in the whole release.
notes: Systemic issues found in ES, in priority order. (1) Coverage hole: the Canaries and Menorca are barely harvested, which is why Teide, Roque Nublo, Las Teresitas, Maspalomas, Papagayo, Sotavento and Macarella are all absent rather than merely mis-ranked. Fixing rank order will not fix this; the harvest must be re-run with island coverage checks. (2) Geocode collapse: beach ranks 241-260 form a 13-row cluster inside a 1 km blob at roughly 38.905/1.423 near Ibiza airport, containing rows named for Cala Comte (real 38.9625/1.22028), Ses Illetes on Formentera (real 38.75/1.4333), Cala d'Hort, Cala Saladeta, Ses Salines and Es Cavallet. Three rows share the exact coordinate 38.89999/1.43333. All 13 carry sources ['eea','osm','whc'] and water 'Good', so the cluster is identifiable by a single query. (3) Duplicate density: I counted 20 beach pairs under 500 m in tier 1/2 that are the same feature under different spellings or languages, plus four rows for Ses Salines and three for La Concha. (4) Wikipedia mis-joins are the mechanism behind most non-beach and non-mountain rows: a stadium article, a palace article, a battle article, a beach article on a mountain row, a peninsula article on a beach row. Validating the linked item's Wikidata P31 against an allowed class list would remove most of them in one pass. (5) The 'unesco' designation is being applied loosely: Platja des Cavallet and the whole Ibiza blob carry it because Ibiza is a UNESCO site, not because the beaches are.
